releases.title: The new app feels more like an app
highlights: Opening an article and going back now slides, and the list is where you left it.
On a phone you can pull the article list or the Feeds list down to refresh it, and the article list shows the last list while the new one loads.
On a phone the screen names are large titles that shrink into a bar as you scroll.
changes: Opening an article from the list slides in, and going back slides out. On a phone, opening a category or a Settings group slides too.
Pull the Articles list down from the top to reload it. If that fails you get a message and the list stays as it was.
Pull the Feeds list down from the top to reload it, on the categories and inside a category. If that fails you get a message and the list stays as it was.

The Articles list shows the list from your last visit straight away and swaps in the new one when it arrives. While nothing is there yet you see grey placeholder lines instead of the word Loading. Signing out or deleting your account clears the saved list.
On a phone, Articles, Feeds and Settings have a large title at the top. When you scroll, the title moves into a small bar over the page.
The tab bar remembers how far you had scrolled in each tab, and tapping the tab you are already on takes you back to the top.
Windows that open from the bottom, such as Send to Kindle setup, now push the page behind them back a little.
Nothing changes on a Kindle, and the older pages are as they were.

releases.title: A calmer article list on Kindle
highlights: On a Kindle the article list is quieter and fits more articles on each page.
Each article shows its title first, with the source and time underneath.
The Send button now says Sent ✓ once an article has gone to your Kindle.
changes: Kindle list: the title comes first and is always shown in full, with the source and the time in one small line below it.
An unread article has a bold title and a small black square in front of the source. The thick bar down the left edge is gone.
Send is an outlined button with the paper plane and the word Send. After an article was sent it reads Sent ✓ with a dashed outline, and you can still tap it to send the article again.
Phones and computers keep the list as it was.

releases.title: Reddit and Hacker News posts come without comments
highlights: Posts from Reddit and Hacker News now open and send as the article only.
The comment threads are no longer pulled in.
changes: Reddit and Hacker News posts are fetched and read like any other article. The comment thread is no longer added to the page, to the EPUB or to what is sent to your Kindle.
When a feed provides a Hacker News comments link, it stays beside Original.
Threads that were already saved with an article stay as they were.

releases.title: The newsletter inbox is gone
highlights: The e-mail address for forwarding newsletters has been removed. No new issues arrive by e-mail.
Newsletters you already received stay readable, and their feeds stay in your list.
changes: The newsletter address is gone from Settings, Kindle, and the "Add a newsletter instead" option is gone from the feed list.
Anything sent to an old newsletter address is no longer received.
Feeds that were created from newsletters keep their articles. You can still read them, send them to Kindle, recategorize them or delete them. They just get no new issues.
A newsletter that publishes an RSS feed can still be followed like any other feed, with Follow a site.

releases.title: Recovery codes, a sign-in link and an install banner
highlights: Create a recovery code under Settings, Account. It is an extra way to sign in, and your password still works.
If you lose the code, the login page can e-mail you a sign-in link. It works once and expires after 20 minutes.
On a phone, Extrablatt now offers to add itself to your home screen.
changes: Settings, Account creates or replaces a recovery code in the form ABCD-EFGH-JKLM. It is shown once, and Extrablatt keeps only a hash of it.
The login page has a "Sign in with a recovery code" option that takes the code alone.
"Lost your recovery code?" on the login page e-mails a one-time sign-in link. The link works once and expires after 20 minutes.
Phones show an install banner. iPhone browsers other than Safari get the Share steps for Add to Home Screen.
Settings, Reading has a new option to mark articles read as you scroll past them. It is off by default and does not apply to Kindle pages.
The Kindle layout is scaled down for newer, high-density Paperwhite screens, so more of the article list fits on one page.

releases.title: Source available, free to self-host
highlights: Extrablatt's source is now public under the PolyForm Noncommercial License.
You can self-host it yourself for personal, noncommercial use, free of charge.
changes: Published the source code under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, with a self-hosting guide in the README.
The marketing site explains self-hosting versus the hosted subscription, and links to the license.

releases.title: Show password on login
highlights: The login form has a "Show password" checkbox.
changes: Checking "Show password" on the login form reveals what was typed instead of dots; the box itself is never sent with the form.

releases.title: Signing up again sends mail
highlights: If the first confirmation e-mail never arrived, signing up again sends a fresh link.
An address that already has an account gets a reminder instead of silence.
changes: Signing up again with an unconfirmed address sends a new confirmation link instead of claiming a message went out and sending nothing.
Signing up with an address that already has a confirmed account mails a reminder with links to log in and to reset the password.
The password from the first sign-up stays in place; the new one typed on a repeat sign-up is ignored.

releases.title: Pages open already styled
highlights: Pages open looking finished instead of a moment of unstyled text first.
Turning a page is lighter: the scripts stay in the browser cache.
changes: The look of a page travels with the page itself, so it does not wait on a second request and does not flash unstyled on a slow connection.
Scripts are cached by their contents, so a page turn no longer downloads them again.

releases.title: Discussions, source address, and send errors
highlights: Reddit and Hacker News posts include comments; replies start collapsed.
Kindle files show the original web address under the title.
If Send to Kindle is refused, the reason shows on the page.
changes: Reddit and Hacker News posts include the discussion; replies start collapsed and expand as a thread.
The Kindle file prints the article's original web address under the title.
Back from an article returns to the same page of the list it was opened from.
After the free week, a notice on login offers Subscribe or Close; Close lasts until the next login.
Subscription says to finish checkout on a phone, not the Kindle.
If Send to Kindle is refused, the reason shows in the page, with a link to Kindle settings when that is what is missing.
Hidden images leave an [Image: caption] marker instead of vanishing.
The article list waits until it has been laid out so the first paint is one page, not a jump.
Turning a page no longer prints how many articles were marked read.
Accounts from before charging began keep sending to Kindle.

releases.title: Easier to follow the news
highlights: Quick start offers newspapers such as BBC, The Guardian, NPR, Tagesschau, and Der Spiegel.
Follow a site by pasting its normal address — no special news link needed.
Send a page to Kindle uses plain language instead of technical terms.
changes: Quick start suggests general newspapers instead of developer sites.
Adding a site asks for a website address and explains that a normal homepage is enough.
Paste an article link to send a page to Kindle; it lands in the library like a book.
If a site cannot be followed, the message says so in plain language.
A feed that fails to update says we will try again, without a technical error dump.

releases.title: Settings pages, Mark read, and your data
highlights: Settings is a list of pages so a Kindle only opens the topic it needs.
Mark a whole feed as read from the category list.
Download or delete everything we hold about the account.
changes: Settings is split into Kindle, Reading, Account, Subscription, Changelog, and Your data.
Your data lets you download a JSON export. Deleting the account removes feeds and articles.
A feed address typed without https:// is accepted.
Until a Kindle address is saved, the Feeds page says where Amazon lists it and how to approve the Extrablatt sender.
From a category, Mark read marks every unread article in that feed.
The article list uses one filter row and fills the screen; the last page of a batch says Mark read and load more.
Imprint, privacy, terms, and withdrawal pages are linked from the footer.

releases.title: Paid plan and a free week
highlights: New accounts get a week of the full plan at no charge.
Supporter is €2.99 a month billed yearly, or €3.99 a month, including VAT.
changes: A new account includes seven days of the full Supporter plan, with no card required.
After that week, reading in the browser stays free; sending to Kindle and adding feeds needs a subscription.
The paid plan is €2.99 a month billed as €35.88 once for 12 months, or €3.99 a month, including VAT. Accounts from before charging began stay free.

releases.title: New send-from address
highlights: Articles and account mail now come from mail@extrablatt.app, labelled Extrablatt.
changes: The shared sender is mail@extrablatt.app instead of a Kindle-branded address. Add that address to Amazon's Approved Personal Document E-mail List or new deliveries will not arrive.

releases.title: Changelog, reading preference, and what's new
highlights: Settings now includes a changelog of recent changes.
After a new release, a short notice highlights what changed.
Marking articles read when you turn the page is a Settings choice.
changes: A changelog in Settings lists recent changes; a popup highlights the most important ones after each new release.
Marking articles as read when you go to the next page can be turned off in Settings. When it is off, new feed articles arrive already marked read so a refresh does not fill Unread with a backlog.
The Older articles list is gone; paging through Articles is the way to go further back.
A category can be renamed even when the new name only differs in capitalization.
The top Refresh button is gone. Feeds still refresh in the background when you open Feeds or Articles, and on the usual schedule.

releases.title: Paste a URL, categories, and e-reader reading
highlights: Send any web page to Kindle by pasting its address on Feeds.
Organize feeds in categories, including renaming a category at once.
Page-at-a-time reading is sized for e-ink screens.
changes: Paste any article URL from Feeds: the page is extracted, stored, and emailed to Kindle like a feed article.
Give feeds a category when adding them, browse by category, and rename a category to move every feed in it.
Page-at-a-time reading and list paging are sized to the device screen so Kindle page turns stay snappy.
Less common article actions sit under More so the reading toolbar stays on one row on small screens.

releases.title: Newsletters and keeping the servers running
highlights: Subscribe to e-mail newsletters with one inbox address per account.
A donation reminder appears every so often after Send-to-Kindle.
changes: Each account can have a newsletter inbox address. Issues show up as articles and send to Kindle like anything else.
A donation link lives in Settings, and a short reminder can appear after every tenth article sent. The app stays free and ad-free either way.
Administrators can see usage telemetry and per-account send limits from Settings.
